title: Interaction-driven electronic ferroelectricity in van der Waals heterostructures
authors: Ziying Wang, Ana Vera Montoto, Mohammad Amini, Yuxiao Ding, Jose L. Lado, Robert Drost, Adolfo O. Fumega, Peter Liljeroth
abstract: Strong electronic correlations in narrow-band systems provide a promising route to realize emergent quantum phases. While ferroelectricity in van der Waals materials is typically associated with inversion symmetry breaking driven by lattice distortions, interlayer sliding, or moiré reconstruction, the possibility of generating ferroelectricity directly from electronic interactions remains largely unexplored. Here, using molecular beam epitaxy, scanning tunneling microscopy, and ab initio calculations, we investigate two stacking geometries of bilayer 1T-TaSe$_2$, A-C and A-C$'$, formed by coupled Star-of-David charge density wave phases. We show that both stackings realize quasi-one-dimensional interacting chains, but are governed by distinct interaction mechanisms. In the A-C stacking, strong interlayer hybridization leads to dimerization and the formation of a band insulating state. In contrast, the A-C$'$ stacking is dominated by interlayer Coulomb interactions, producing a spontaneous charge imbalance between layers that gives rise to an out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization. Furthermore, we demonstrate that ferroelectric and antiferroelectric interchain configurations can be stabilized and electrically switched by an external field. Our results prove that bilayer 1T-TaSe$_2$ is a platform for interaction-driven electronic ferroelectricity, establishing an overlooked family of charge-ordered correlated states in 1T-TaSe$_2$ multilayers.
summary: The authors demonstrate that electronic correlations, rather than structural distortions, can induce ferroelectricity in bilayer 1T-TaSe2. By comparing two stacking arrangements (A-C and A-C'), they show the A-C' stack develops a polar charge density wave phase. This establishes a new platform for studying interaction-driven correlated quantum states.
main_problem: The study investigates generating ferroelectricity directly from electronic interactions, bypassing traditional structural symmetry breaking mechanisms common in van der Waals (vdW) materials.
main_result: Bilayer 1T-TaSe2 exhibits interaction-driven electronic ferroelectricity in the A-C' stacking geometry, which can be electrically switched between antiferroelectric and ferroelectric CDW states.
method: The research combines first-principles DFT calculations with a minimal tight-binding model solved via mean-field approximation, complemented by STM/STS measurements on MBE-grown samples.
model_or_system: The system is bilayer 1T-TaSe2, modeled as quasi-one-dimensional interacting chains governed by a Hamiltonian including hopping ($H_0$), onsite repulsion ($H_U$), and interlayer Coulomb interactions ($H_V$). Two stacking geometries (A-C and A-C') are compared.
key_observables: Out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization, electronic band structure (insulating vs. CDW), charge modulation patterns observed via STM/STS ($	ext{dI/dV}$ spectra).
important_parameters: Interlayer Coulomb interaction strength ($V$), dimerization parameter ($\delta t_{\perp}$), and external electric field bias ($\Delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a mean-field approximation for solving the full interacting Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate STM images of A-C and A-C' bilayers, DFT band structures showing insulating/CDW states, and phase diagrams mapping out correlated electronic phases based on interaction strengths.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares two stacking geometries (A-C vs. A-C') using theoretical modeling and experimental characterization to demonstrate how interlayer interactions dictate the emergent ferroic order.
why_interesting: This work provides a clear example of correlation effects driving macroscopic polarization in 2D materials, which is highly relevant for understanding correlated quantum states beyond simple band theory predictions.
